items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: it's Martin Luther King now, from Claiborne on down to Dry. I never did go in that direction.

ctx.x: We're up to reel number seven. We're up to number seven on Tommy Ridgler. Okay, and we're talking about Carnival and how it's changed.

Oh yeah, well, what I was talking about, the Black Carnival downtown on Arlene Street. You see, I mean, from Arlene and Claiborne on down to Arlene and St. Bernard, this was a Carnival, and then on Melford, I never did go on Melford Mean Street from, well, it's Martin Luther King now, from Claiborne on down to Dry. I never did go in that direction. I always went down and down. And from there, I walked Claiborne Street, and then I would go on Connell Street. But, you know, I wish some people had filmed that era of…
